APPROVE
`JudgeAsync` now has roughly ten flat branches and ternaries, well under 15; every early-return verdict, its order and its arguments are preserved across the extracted stages; and the changes compile cleanly (local-function shadowing, the `Report!` null-forgiving, the nullable switch expression), assuming `ScoreAsync`/`BenchAtPinAsync` return `Task<string?>` as `BaseArmAsync` declares, which I could not check without the repository.
